q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE,VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID)>1 ORDER BY VIEWER_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE,VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID)>1 ORDER BY VIEWER_ID
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (2, 102, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (3, 103, 202, '2023-01-01');
explanation: Q1 orders the results by ID, while Q2 orders the results by VIEWER_ID. Since VIEWER_ID and ID are the same column, this difference in order by clause does not change the result in this specific case. However, if the column names were different, this could lead to different results.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have multiple viewers with the same number of distinct articles viewed on the same date. The difference in order by clause should result in different output.
